title: Counting in nilpotent injectors and Carter subgroups: the divisibility counterexample for Carter subgroups (Theorem D)
author: S. Aivazidis, M. Loukaki and J. Shareshian
work: Counting in nilpotent injectors and Carter subgroups
difficulty_reason: Supplying the paper's own prerequisites - the structure of the affine group A = A Gamma L_1(2^p) with A = JMV, the centraliser computations in the semidirect product G = AW, the Carter subgroup machinery for soluble groups, and the counting identity for the number of Carter subgroups containing a fixed element - still leaves a 135-line constructive proof that is not a qualifying-examination exercise. The proof must build the specific soluble group G = AW with W an F_p-vector space with basis indexed by the field F of order 2^p, verify that H = J V_2 C_W(V_2) is nilpotent and self-normalising in G so that H is Carter, compute its order and the index (G:H), then establish the divisibility of the number of Carter subgroups containing the element e_X by counting in two ways the pairs (s,C) with s in the conjugacy class of e_X and C Carter containing s, and finally derive the exact divisibility of the class intersection from the transitivity of the multiplicative group on the index-two subgroups and from Fermat's Little Theorem. Every step is a source-local group-theoretic construction and count rather than a quotation from a textbook, so the unit is well beyond ordinary PhD qualification problems in group theory.
